A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLRF research. Their full text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across pagination and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Im2SVG and Text2SVG experiments, benchmark comparisons, ablations and qualitative analyses in the main text and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results, adds baseline comparisons, and reports a human evaluation of SVG fidelity and editability in Appendix A.6.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the stated DreamSim reward from R = 1 - 2 sim with sim in [-1,1] to sim = 1 - cos in [0,2] and R = 1 - sim. This changes the specified reward component; the architectures and SFT–GRPO pipeline remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Im2SVG and Text2SVG coverage: SVG-Stack/Stack-Hard, SVG-Emoji, SVG-Fonts, SVG-Icons, Flickr30k, MM-Icon and MM-Illustration. The new human evaluation uses 50 existing SVG-Stack-Hard examples, adding an assessment procedure rather than a new generation task or input domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated Im2VEC and SuperSVG rows on SVG-Stack-Hard. Table 4 adds LLM4SVG-GPT2XL (3B) across the three Text2SVG benchmarks. Existing comparators are retained, making this a limited expansion of already broad comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix A.6 adds anonymized, randomized paired-output human judgments of fidelity and editability on 50 examples, reporting 267 evaluations. Existing training budgets, metrics and inference settings remain unchanged. The new study's participant count is inconsistent: 18 in the text versus 19 in Figure 14.

E4.justification: Appendix A.6 adds a supplementary human assessment of whether RLRF improves fidelity and editability, including designer observations about SVG organization. Existing SFT, reward, temperature, rollout and KL ablations, generalization analyses and reward-hacking cases are retained.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged: neither version supplies experimental confidence intervals, significance tests or seed-based variability estimates. The new human-study vote counts, percentages and agreement/tie summary are descriptive results, without an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises Qwen2.5-VL-7B RLRF under the retained stated evaluation: MSE 4.01 to 1.03, SSIM 89.18 to 95.10, DINO 96.31 to 98.70, LPIPS 9.74 to 3.08, and code efficiency -248 to -334. It now surpasses LIVE on MSE and LPIPS; the reason for these revisions is unexplained. Tables 1 and 4 add comparator results. Table 4 changes Gemini-Flash-2.0's Flickr30k Accurate/Aesthetic scores from 87.00/99.00 to 1.87/2.23. The new human study reports RLRF preferences of 42.7% for fidelity and 59.2% for editability.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the semantic score's mathematical definition, range and reward mapping, making the stated reward bounded in [-1,1] and increasing with cosine alignment. This is a mathematical correction, not merely notation. Other objectives and equations are retained, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about rendering-feedback RL, composite rewards, generalization, fidelity and compactness. Added comparisons and human judgments provide support for existing contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix A.6 newly interprets fidelity ties as evidence that SFT handles straightforward examples well, while attributing RLRF's advantages to harder cases and cleaner, more interpretable SVG structure. Existing limitations concerning complex inputs, context length, specialization and rollout cost remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Sections 4.1 and Appendices B–C retain the same software stack, preprocessing, optimizer settings, hardware, training times, frozen vision tower, reward-hacking mitigations and best-of-five inference details. No new implementation or code/data access information accompanies the revised benchmark scores or added baselines.

R1.justification: Appendices D.2–D.3 add discussion and citations concerning SCOPE, computer-use grounding and GRPO for image editing. The central positioning against supervised SVG generation and execution-focused RL remains intact. Additional StepCoder and PPOCoder bibliography entries duplicate works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v2 adds Appendix A.6 and its contents entry, locally rewrites the semantic-reward and extended-related-work passages, corrects two RLVG references to RLRF, and updates the conference header. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the human-study summary as Figure 14, expands Tables 1 and 4, and adds score highlighting in Tables 4–5. Earlier Figures 14–15 are retained as Figures 15–16. Existing diagrams, plots and qualitative illustrations remain unchanged, with local page reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the inconsistent DreamSim formulation and out-of-range Gemini judge scores, while additional comparators and human judgments modestly strengthen validation. These gains are limited by unexplained changes to the central 7B results and inconsistent study reporting: Appendix A.6 lists 18 participants and four model variants, whereas Figure 14 shows 19 users and only Qwen comparisons. The corrections and broader evidence provide a modest net improvement, without establishing that the larger reported performance gains are better substantiated.
